newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shanghai Ind becomes real Shanghai concept.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Ind becomes real Shanghai concept.

text.p: Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd will be transformed into a true Shanghai concept company after completion of the recently announced asset injections, chairman Cai Laixing said on Monday.

The HK$2.7 billion asset injections of Shanghai Industrial, a locally incorporated company controlled by the Shanghai municipal government, would lift the proportion of its Shanghai investment to 56 percent of the company's total investment from the current 10 percent, Cai told a news conference.
"The Shanghai concept stock has started to get its shape gradually," he said.
Hong Kong investment would be diluted to 44 percent from 90 percent after the purchase of the six Shanghai projects, the chairman said.

Its Hong Kong tobacco business would continue to be the company's largest single bread winner in 1997 while it would be followed by automobile component manufacturing venture Shanghai Huizhong Automotive, managing director Chen Weishu said.
The venture company posted a net profit of HK$242.8 million in the first eight months of the year against HK$288.47 for the whole of 1995.
"We see steady growth for the company next year," Chen said but declined to give a specific figure.
SI Infrastructure Holdings Ltd which holds 50.2 percent of Shanghai Yanan Road Elevated Road Development Co Ltd, would become the third profit contributor next year.
Chen said the municipal government guaranteed the internal rate of return of about 14 percent at least for the western and eastern sections of the Yanan Road Elevated Highway.

The remaining new acquisitions, Shanghai Bright Dairy and Food Co Ltd, Shanghai Orient Shopping Centre Ltd, Shanghai Transportation Electric Joint Venture and Shanghai daily chemical plant would also have significant contributions next year, he added.

The 1996 price/earnings ratio of the company's shares was currently at 32-33 times and it should be lowered to 27 times after the acquisitions and further decline to about 19 times on projected 1997 earnings, the chairman said.
